note: Slack posts to Slack.com via an Incoming Webhook. Config object slack.settings: slack_webhook_url (required), slack_channel, slack_username, slack_icon_type/emoji/url, slack_link_names, slack_queue_messages. Settings form slack.admin_settings at /admin/config/services/slack/config; test form slack.admin_test. Service slack.slack_service (Slack/SlackInterface): deliverMessage() (queues or sends per slack_queue_messages), sendMessage() (immediate), queueMessage() (enqueue to slack_message QueueWorker). Rules action rules_slack_send_message. No own permissions/Drush/plugin-types. Because a real webhook/token the agent won't have is required to actually deliver, ALL evals are grounded in the module's own slack.settings config — no message is ever sent to Slack.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with the slack module, which service and method do I call from custom code to send a message to Slack, and what is the difference between deliverMessage(), sendMessage() and queueMessage()?
evals.expected_output: Use the slack.slack_service service (Slack/SlackInterface). deliverMessage() honours the slack_queue_messages setting (queues or sends), sendMessage() posts immediately via the webhook, queueMessage() enqueues to the slack_message queue worker for cron. All take ($message, $channel='', $username='', $webhook_url=NULL).

evals.prompt: What does the slack module need to actually deliver messages, where is that configured (config object + route), and what permission guards it?
evals.expected_output: It needs an Incoming Webhook URL stored as slack.settings.slack_webhook_url, set on the Slack configuration form at /admin/config/services/slack/config (route slack.admin_settings), guarded by the 'administer site configuration' permission. Without a webhook nothing is delivered.

evals.prompt: Can a site builder post to Slack from the Rules module using the slack module without writing code? What is the Rules action's id/label?
evals.expected_output: Yes: the module ships a Rules action 'Send message to Slack' (id rules_slack_send_message, category Slack) with Message/Channel/User name context, so you can post to Slack from a Rules reaction. It requires the drupal/rules module.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the slack module is configured. Inspect the live slack configuration and report the default channel and bot username it will post as.
evals.expected_output: slack.settings has slack_channel = '#ops-intro' and slack_username = 'IntroBot'. Discoverable via `drush cget slack.settings` (slack_channel, slack_username).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the slack module is configured with an incoming webhook. Inspect the live slack configuration and report the webhook host/URL it will post to.
evals.expected_output: slack.settings.slack_webhook_url is set to https://hooks.slack.com/services/T00INTRO/B00INTRO/introplaceholder (host hooks.slack.com). Discoverable via `drush cget slack.settings slack_webhook_url`.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the slack module to post to the channel #slack-task as the bot 'TaskBot' using the incoming webhook https://hooks.slack.com/services/T00000000/B00000000/taskplaceholdertoken, and enable message queueing so messages are sent on cron. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: slack.settings has slack_webhook_url set to the given hooks.slack.com URL, slack_channel = '#slack-task', slack_username = 'TaskBot', and slack_queue_messages = true (set via the settings form or config factory).

evals.prompt: I want my Drupal site to drop messages into our Slack #slack-task channel as a bot called TaskBot. Here is the Slack incoming webhook address: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T00000000/B00000000/taskplaceholdertoken . Please set that up, and make it send the messages in the background (on cron) rather than instantly. Save it live.
evals.expected_output: Same end state as the expert phrasing: slack.settings webhook set to the given URL, slack_channel '#slack-task', slack_username 'TaskBot', slack_queue_messages true.
